routes.label: Read the scale as a number line

question:
The diagram shows part of a scale of a measuring device. The arrow indicates an approximate reading of

[Figure 1](figures/1988_AMC_8_Q01_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
Imagine straightening the curved scale into a number line, preserving the order and equal spacing of the marks. Place the indicated point the same fraction of the way between its neighboring marks. This preserves the reading because equal gaps still represent equal increases in value.

The three interior marks divide the interval from \(10\) to \(11\) into four equal gaps. Each gap represents
\[
(11-10)\div4=0.25.
\]
Thus the marked values on the number line are
\[
10,\quad 10.25,\quad 10.50,\quad 10.75,\quad 11.
\]
The arrow points slightly beyond \(10.25\), approximately one fifth of the way toward \(10.50\). One fifth of a gap represents \(0.25\div5=0.05\), so the approximate reading is
\[
10.25+0.05=\boxed{10.3}.
\]
Therefore the answer is \(\text{D}\).
